2026-08-28.headline: Score HOLDS at 27/30 for a fourteenth consecutive edition. No channel moved. The day’s finding is that the mine claim is now contradicted on the OPERATIONAL record, and that Iran answered the mediators by naming a price rather than a route. One. JMIC Update 090 (ICOD 271500Z August), published by UKMTO on 27 August, states verbatim that “there remained a continued risk of drifting or uncharted mines in and near the TSS, with mine danger areas still active” — and adds that “clearance and mine-surveying operations continue throughout the Strait of Hormuz, with updated coordinates and graphics available from NAVCENT NCAGS”. Two days after the President of the United States declared that all mines had been removed from the international waters of the Strait, an allied advisory records mine danger areas as still active and refers merchant shipping to NAVCENT NCAGS for the coordinates. That narrows the standing three-way dispute but does not close it: 090 is an allied product carrying a NAVCENT referral, not a NAVCENT statement, and no US Navy, CENTCOM or NAVCENT text addressing the presidential claim has issued. The operational record and the political claim do not agree; the operational record is the American one. Two. UKMTO Attack 121-26 was issued on 27 August for an incident of 25 August: the tanker AL SALAM II, transiting EASTBOUND INSIDE the Strait near Khasab, struck above the waterline by an unknown projectile, fire extinguished, all crew safe — confirmed by the OMANI Maritime Security Centre at 262350Z. The cumulative incident count moves 96 to 97. The publication lag is itself the finding: Tehran made the corridor and revenue-sharing announcements of 26 August the day AFTER a vessel had been struck inside the Strait, and the day BEFORE any public record of that strike existed. No party has claimed the attack and no government has attributed it. Three. Iran named a price. SNSC Secretary Mohsen Rezaei, to Al Manar and relayed by Reuters on 27 August: Iran is drafting a LIST OF CONDITIONS for reopening the Strait at the mediators’ request, with “ending the regional war” among them, and ships would use a “designated central channel” only if the United States met those conditions. That is the THIRD Iranian description of the arrangement in TWO days — Gharibabadi’s entry through Iranian territorial waters, the IRGC’s agreed share of waters and revenues, and now a central channel; two are geometries and one is a revenue claim, and none of the three has an Omani counterpart, because the 25 August joint STATEMENT — the only text either government has published — describes no geometry, no fee and no revenue share. A senior Iranian source told Reuters on 26 August the two sides were “still working on details”. All Tier 3, all relayed; relay is not corroboration. Four. Qatar’s prime minister went to Tehran on 27 August carrying a position incompatible with the framework itself. He met Araghchi, Pezeshkian and Ghalibaf; Doha’s stated object, per its own spokesman, is freedom of navigation and a return to the status quo PRIOR TO 28 FEBRUARY — an international waterway under the IMO traffic separation scheme, which is the negation of a jointly administered, revenue-sharing Strait. AND A STANDING PREMISE OF THIS DOCUMENT IS NARROWED: the last two editions wrote that the un-issued joint DECLARATION — a later and different instrument from the 25 August joint STATEMENT, which WAS issued — is “Qatar’s gate on all mediation”. Nothing published in this window supports that; Qatar engaged on 27 August with the framework still only “discussed”. The claim was load-bearing, it was inherited, and it is cut back to what the record shows. Five, and Washington disowned the track on the record the same day. White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt, 27 August: “No negotiations are happening right now, and this will continue until the president feels that maybe they come to the table in a meaningful way. We have not seen that yet.” She named the two campaigns — Operation Epic Fury militarily and Operation Economic Outcast economically — and confirmed the naval blockade continues. Six, and it is the market half. The 27 August Singapore snapshot missed the ENTIRE US session in ONE direction, and FOUR of this document’s readings are withdrawn by name — three because of the snapshot and one because of a restatement. Brent settled $2.10 above the snapshot and the active $2.47, and the whole 2- to 30-year sector +1.03 to +1.76 bp; Henry Hub and TTF are EXCLUDED from the reconciliation, because their gaps mix a timing miss with the restatement and measure neither. Brent ROSE $1.58 to $88.52, ending the down-run at three, and the upgrade gap NARROWED to $6.48 from $8.06 — the opposite of what the last edition led on. The four withdrawals are: (a) the three-session down-run together with the “second consecutive widening” to $8.06; (b) the intraday claim that the 30-year failed Threshold B by 1.73 bp, which settled at 0.69; (c) “§9.15 is restored”, which described 26 August and does not describe 27 August; and (d) “Henry Hub 7.22% below pre-war”, the one withdrawal the Singapore cut did NOT cause. Seven. Threshold B did not re-arm, and it has never been closer on the binding leg: the 30-year fails by 0.69 bp — the narrowest 30-year-leg miss recorded ON A CLOSE — while the 10-year is SATISFIED at 4.6762%. The fifth lapse is now three closes old, 25 to 27 August; the ordinals are recomputed and unchanged at the TENTH state and the NINTH change. Eight. The rotation rule does NOT fire on 27 August, and saying so is the point of stating it. The two Treasury downgrade legs did not rotate — they BOTH moved away: MOVE rose 0.42 to 69.86, still an EIGHTH consecutive close below 75 but by less, while the yield leg widened 2.60 bp to 19.31. The last such joint deterioration was 21 August. US-inflation therefore REMAINS the nearer of the two market downgrade candidates, as it was a session ago, and the distance between them widened from 0.59 bp to 1.69. Nine. The $44bn 7-year cleared at 4.512% on a 2.50 cover with dealers at 12.264% of competitive-accepted — a FIFTH consecutive coupon auction with a backstop in single or low double digits, and the SECOND-HIGHEST of the five, behind the 20-year’s 12.34%. The run is intact; it is not tightening. Ten. Diesel’s run of war highs BROKE: AAA diesel fell 0.47 cents to $5.6183 after four consecutive war highs — none of them an all-time record, which is 19.76 cents higher — and regular is now BELOW both its week-ago and its month-ago level. The scored AUTMUSAG series is DARK on 27 August with its 28 August print PROSPECTIVE, and its 26 August value backfilled at $4.83, IDENTICAL to 25 August’s — so it is reported UNRESOLVED, not as a print. Eleven, and it is a data-integrity finding. A vendor RESTATEMENT occurred, confined to the gas complex: Henry Hub and TTF were restated UPWARD across 24, 25 and 26 August and every other field is unrestated. This document’s own “Henry Hub 7.22% below pre-war” now reads 6.17% on the restated 26 August close — a number that moved without the market moving. analysis.bondYieldNote: Six channels, in the order in which they moved rather than in scoring order. bondYield.title: (i) Treasury stress — held at 5 (max), and the rotation rule does NOT apply this session
bondYield.text: The last edition recorded the two downgrade legs ROTATING apart on 26 August. On 27 August they did not rotate: BOTH moved away from the downgrade. MOVE ROSE 0.42 to 69.86 — still below 75 and therefore still satisfying its leg, but by 5.14 points instead of 5.56 — while the yield leg widened 2.60 bp from 16.71 to 19.31. A joint deterioration is not a rotation and must not be described as one; the previous joint deterioration was 21 August. The rotation rule has a third state and it is named here rather than forced. The volatility leg is a regime and remains one, but state it precisely: MOVE has closed below 75 on eight consecutive sessions, 18 through 27 August — the longest run since 10 June to 10 July, against an intervening maximum of five sessions, 15–21 July. The wider sub-75 PHASE dates from 12 August and was broken by a single close of 75.63 on 17 August, which is why the unbroken RUN starts on 18 August. 69.86 is only the FOURTH-lowest close of that phase, behind 69.23 (13 August), 69.44 (26 August) and 69.58 (14 August), and it is not close to the WAR low of 65.39 set on 18 June. The yield leg fails and it failed by more, and the arithmetic of how far is now unfavourable: the rule requires a 30-year close below 5.00% SUSTAINED, and 19.31 bp is more than twice the largest single-session 30-year move since 1 August, which is the 9.15 bp fall of 19 August. The last four sessions moved 4.64, 5.94, 0.20 and 2.60, so the yield leg is three or more sessions away on any reasonable reading, having been two to three a session ago. The honest summary of 27 August is that the whole curve sold off with the belly leading — 2-year +2.27 bp, 5-year +3.77, 10-year +2.97, 30-year +2.60 — which is neither the front-end Fed repricing of 26 August nor a term-premium session. It is a curve that sold off on labour-market data and an auction, with the Gulf absent from the attribution for a second consecutive session.

bondYield.title: (ii) US inflation impulse — held at 5 (max), and the level whose break fired it has been reclaimed for two closes
bondYield.text: The 5y5y forward closed 2.3182% on 27 August, a SECOND consecutive close above the 2.30% level whose sustained break fired this channel from 4 to 5 on 31 July, and 1.82 bp clear of it. Bound that properly: there have been exactly TWO single closes BELOW 2.30% in the current regime — 13 August and 25 August — and BOTH were retraced inside one session. Neither was a regime and neither moved a channel; the confirmed-close discipline has now been vindicated twice on the same level, and a channel moved on either close would have been wrong within twenty-four hours. The documented downgrade is a sustained close at or below the 2.142% pre-war anchor, and the gap WIDENED to 17.62 bp from 16.12. The rule has not been moved to meet the trigger and the distance between the two is published rather than closed. The corroborating series moved the same way: ten-year breakeven compensation closed 2.3335%, 7.66 bp above its 2.2569% pre-war anchor, from 6.91. The forward and the realised data have now converged on the same reading, which is a change from the previous session. July PCE landed hot on the headline on 26 August — +0.2% m/m and +3.7% y/y against +0.1% and 3.6% consensus, core in line, real spending FLAT, with gasoline and other energy goods the largest single POSITIVE goods contributor at +$16.4bn inside a $49.9bn goods decline — and on 27 August the compensation market moved up to meet it rather than fading it. Consumers are cutting everything except the thing the war made expensive, and for the first time in this regime the forward market is pricing that as more than a relative-price event. The channel holds at 5 on the documented rule; the composition is what a reader should watch. On the numbers, US inflation REMAINS the nearer of the two market downgrade candidates at 17.62 bp against Treasury’s 19.31 — it was already nearer a session ago at 16.12 against 16.71, and the distance between them widened from 0.59 bp to 1.69. Nothing swapped.

bondYield.title: (iii) Oil price shock — held at 2, and the upgrade gap NARROWED after two widenings
bondYield.text: The sequence of edition-over-edition distances to the $95 upgrade reads 9.78, 8.43, 5.55, 5.21, 3.03, 7.73, 8.06, 6.48 on the scored CO2 series — eight readings, five narrowings, two widenings — and on the active contract $7.16 to $5.30. Brent’s three-session down-run ENDED at three: it closed +$1.58 at $88.52 on 27 August and printed $88.13 intraday on 28 August. The last edition led on the down-run and on a second consecutive widening; the settled close reversed both, and the reversal is a failure of the Singapore snapshot rather than a change of view — it is withdrawn by name in the reconciliation. No named, dated attribution for the 27 August move could be sourced, and none is asserted. What can be stated is the physical record standing beside the price: US commercial crude 428.9 mn bbl, essentially unchanged, on crude imports of 6.2 mb/d against a 6.6 four-week average; distillate about 14% below its five-year average and gasoline about 14% below on the EIA’s own wording; and Kpler putting Chinese imports of Iranian crude routed through the Strait at about 530 kb/d across July and August combined, 48% below pre-war. THE SPR FIGURE NOW HAS TWO PUBLISHED VALUES THAT DO NOT RECONCILE, AND BOTH ARE PRINTED: this monitor recorded 289.7 mn bbl, while the DOE’s own SPR Quick Facts page, last modified 24 August, gives a crude-oil-inventory-by-site total of 294.1 MMB as of 20 August. The downgrade needs a mediated pause AND a close at or below $72.48; the price leg is $16.04 away and WIDENED by $1.58 on the session — name the leg: a rising Brent moves toward the upgrade and away from the downgrade, and this session did both.

bondYield.title: (iv) Political stress — held at 5 (max), and the scored series is UNRESOLVED then dark
bondYield.text: The scored AUTMUSAG all-grades series last printed a RESOLVED $4.83 on 25 August — 23 cents above the named $4.60 downgrade condition and eight cents above the $4.75 trigger that fired the upgrade. Its 26 August cell, reported blank last edition, has BACKFILLED at $4.83 — identical to 25 August. The exact-equality rule binds: a field identical to its predecessor at the extract’s full precision is UNRESOLVED and no day-on-day change may be asserted for it, regardless of whether the row around it is live. The distance to the $4.60 condition is 23 cents whether the cell is read as a print or discarded, so nothing turns on it — which is why it is the right session to apply the rule cleanly. The honest qualification is that AUTMUSAG is a two-decimal series that has repeated values genuinely, $4.82 having run on four consecutive sessions from 19 to 24 August, so the test discriminates less here than on a yield. The series is DARK on 27 August and its 28 August value is PROSPECTIVE, and no trend is read through either. The direct reads turned down. And the diesel record run BROKE. It is still +7.06 cents on the week and +32.22 on the month, so the level and the trend remain a freight-fuel shock; what broke is the run of records, and the deceleration this document flagged a session early was correct. bondYield.title: (v) Maritime denial — held at 5 (max), and the most consequential datum is documentary rather than numerical
bondYield.text: The downgrade needs a verified reopening plus traffic above 25% of the UKMTO/JMIC ~138/day all-transit baseline for ten sessions. JMIC Update 090 restates that baseline in its own text and then gives the counts against it: 6 vessels on 25 August and 5 on 26 August on the S&P/SeaVision annex — 4.3% and 3.6% of the scored divisor — with the prose reading “single-digit numbers transiting in both directions”. Name every denominator, and do not add the two American series: the same document reports 37 US NCAGS-FACILITATED transits across the 25–26 August 48 hours, which is a facilitated subset on a different population and runs about three times the annex total for the same 48 hours; they are printed side by side and never summed. Kpler via Reuters counts 10 VISIBLE vessels on 26 August against its own ~15 ten-day average — and its 25 August figure now reads 8 on the visible-vessel basis where the last edition carried 5 on the commodity-vessel basis; that is a different Kpler series, not a revision, and no delta is computed across them. Windward publishes two counts for the same 26 August day, 12 and 8, the second on a stated 21:00–21:00 UTC window with an exclusion rule; both are Windward’s. Al Jazeera, 27 August, puts the 15 July to 23 August average at about five vessels a day, roughly 95% below its own stated ~100/day pre-war baseline — a further divisor, quoted with its own basis. The 25% test runs on the scored annex counts alone, and at 4.3% and 3.6% they are about a sixth of it; the other universes are not the scored one and no test runs on them. The most consequential datum is documentary. JMIC 090 describes the two lanes as operationally EXISTING — “the northern Iranian-controlled route” and “the southern Omani corridor” — and warns that vessels transiting with AIS on “can expect to receive directed hails instructing them to divert toward the northern Iranian-controlled route”. Read that precisely: it is advice about what vessels can EXPECT, not a log of instances, and no hailed or diverted vessel is named. What it does establish is that an allied military product already treats the two-lane architecture as the working environment and the northern lane as Iranian-controlled, before any instrument has been published. On that reading the corridor is the reason this channel cannot move on a communiqué.

bondYield.title: (vi) Escalation risk — held at 5 (max); the kinetic case is the strongest recorded and the DIPLOMATIC case moved backwards on the record
bondYield.text: State the kinetic case at full strength. FOUR separate clocks, never merged: CENTCOM’s combat-release silence has reached 30 days; 28 consecutive nights with no US or Israeli strike inside Iran; 8 with no Iranian ballistic launch; 9 with no drone launch. JMIC Update 090 records no confirmed attack or disruption on shipping in the Arabian Gulf, Gulf of Oman, Arabian Sea, Gulf of Aden, Southern Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb or Northern Red Sea in the reporting period — the Strait of Hormuz is NOT among them. A Tier 2 claim that no launch by ANY party occurred anywhere in theatre on 27 August is NOT CARRIED and is withdrawn: three Houthi ballistic missiles struck Mocha port on 26 August and a fourth hit Khokha on 27 August. The four clocks above are about Iran and the United States and are unaffected by it. Alongside the kinetic silence: no OFAC Iran action on 27 or 28 August, the 27 August action being Venezuela-only, and Qatar’s prime minister physically in Tehran. It is held, and the announcement rule is the reason — but the reason is now stated by the parties rather than inferred. The White House said on the record on 27 August that “no negotiations are happening right now” and that this “will continue until the president feels that maybe they come to the table in a meaningful way”, naming Operation Epic Fury and Operation Economic Outcast and confirming the blockade continues. Iran, the same day, said it is drafting CONDITIONS — “ending the regional war” among them — and that the central channel opens only if the US complies, while the IRGC restated that the Strait does not reopen until Washington lifts the blockade, pays compensation and removes sanctions. Two parties publicly setting preconditions on the same day that a mediator visits is not a stand-down; it is a priced stalemate. And the physical record cuts against the downgrade on its own: a tanker was struck INSIDE the Strait on 25 August, published only on 27 August, unclaimed and unattributed, and it is that incident which moved the count 96 to 97 — 090’s regional summaries record no NEW attack on shipping in the 26–27 August window. JMIC 090’s mine language is unamended and it refers shipping to NAVCENT for current mine-danger coordinates, and it advises that vessels can expect to be hailed and directed onto the Iranian route. A tanker struck inside the waterway on the EVE of the corridor announcements, published only the day AFTER them and two days after the strike itself, is the clearest available measure of the distance between the instrument and the water.

stage4.title: Threshold A · a failed-auction test — NOT ARMED, and UNTESTABLE AS WRITTEN
stage4.text: A is a failed-auction test — an auction clearing with a tail above its when-issued level — and Treasury publishes no when-issued level at all, so no first-party Treasury source can ever confirm a tail. The clearing statistics are the substitute and they are reachable every time. The $44bn 7-year note (CUSIP 91282CRJ2), auctioned 27 August, cleared at a high yield of 4.512% on a bid-to-cover of 2.50, with 97.63% of the competitive award allotted at the high; price 99.928654, coupon 4.500%, median 4.460%, low 4.350%. Name the denominator: primary dealers took 12.264% of competitive-accepted and 12.234% of total award ex-SOMA; directs 26.959% and 26.893%; indirects 60.777% and 60.631%. Competitive tenders were $110.1bn against $43.9bn accepted, with a $5.66bn SOMA add-on outside the award. Tendered by class, dealers put in $59.5bn, directs $18.6bn and indirects $32.0bn — dealers tendered the most and took the least, which is the mechanical shape of a backstop that was not needed. This is the FIFTH consecutive COUPON auction to clear with a dealer backstop in single or low double digits — 12.34% on the 20-year, 2.09% on the 30-year TIPS, 10.90% on the 2-year, 10.05% on the 5-year and 12.264% here, all five on the competitive-accepted denominator so the run sits on one basis; a TIPS is a coupon security, which is why it belongs, and the FRN is not, which is why it never does. BUT SAY WHICH WAY IT MOVED: 12.264% is the SECOND-HIGHEST of the five, behind the 20-year’s 12.34%, and the five span 2.09% to 12.34%. The run is intact; it is NOT tightening, and no trend within it is asserted. The direct share at 26.959% is again large in absolute terms; no trailing average for this tenor is published here, so no composition change is asserted. The $28bn 2-year FRN’s 33.08% dealer take is structurally higher on floating-rate paper and is never spliced into the coupon series. Source: the Fiscal Data auctions API, read directly; the TreasuryDirect PDF endpoint returned empty.

stage4.title: Threshold B · 30Y above 5.20% with 10Y above 4.65% — STILL LAPSED on a third close, and never closer on the binding leg
stage4.text: On the 27 August close the 10-year is SATISFIED at 4.6762%, clearing by 2.62 bp after failing by 0.35 bp the session before, and ONLY the 30-year fails — at 5.1931%, short by 0.69 bp. The two are not the same claim. The ordinals are recomputed from the printed sequence every edition and are UNCHANGED, because no state changed: armed 29 Jul–3 Aug, out 4–5, in 6, out 7, in 10–12, out 13, in 14–18, out 19, in 20–24, out 25–27 — five armings, five lapses, TEN states and NINE changes. This is the FIFTH lapse, now three closes old, and a re-arm would be the SIXTH arming. Eight of the previous nine states lasted three closes or fewer and four lasted exactly one, so a three-close lapse already matches the longest state since 29 July other than the opening four-close arming. On the 28 August intraday the 10-year still satisfies at 4.6703% and the 30-year fails by 0.59 bp. The standing inference holds: 4.65% and 5.20% are the middle of the distribution, not its edge.

stage4.title: Threshold C · MOVE above 130 — not armed, and the pairing WIDENED
stage4.text: MOVE closed 69.86, some 60.14 points below the 130 trigger. Bound it: this is not the furthest MOVE has been from C in the war — the war low is 65.39 on 18 June — and it is not the lowest close of the sub-75 phase begun on 12 August, which is 69.23 on 13 August, nor the second- or third-lowest, which are 69.44 (26 August) and 69.58 (14 August). The war high of 115.02 (26 March) is 45.16 points away. The pairing is the point and it WIDENED: MOVE sits 3.52 points BELOW its pre-war anchor while the 30-year sits 58.25 bp ABOVE its own, a combined divergence of 61.77 against 59.59 a session earlier. A fully normalised expectation of movement priced around a yield that has not normalised at all — and on 27 August both legs moved FURTHER from their anchors at once.

The measure rests on the UAE defence ministry’s attribution to Iran of two ballistic missiles detected on 18 August, which Tehran denies and has not withdrawn the denial of, and NO US or CENTCOM statement corroborating the Emirati assessment had been published as of 27 August — a tenth day. IRAN’S DOMESTIC TRANSMISSION, recorded as context and deliberately NOT used to move a probability. The fuel position was described in terms of impossibility by two vice-presidents, in public and on the record: Executive Vice President Mohammad Jafar Ghaempanah — “continuing on this path is impossible”, with domestic gasoline production insufficient and the US naval blockade preventing imports; First Vice President Mohammadreza Aref — importing substandard gasoline is not a sustainable solution. Consumption runs about 135 mn litres a day against roughly 121 mn of refinery and petrochemical output; queues blocked streets in Tehran and Mashhad on 25 and 26 August; a price rise and a rationing scheme are signalled within weeks against a subsidised structure whose lowest tier is 15,000 rials a litre. A single-stream opposition outlet reports strategic reserve drawdown at a level officials describe as red alert with stocks possibly exhausted within weeks — Tier 3, single-stream, reported and NOT relied on. The rial is around 2.02 mn to the dollar on the open market against an official rate near 1.5 mn, with Statistical Centre inflation near 90%. PETROL PRICING IS THE PRECISE TRIGGER OF THE NOVEMBER 2019 PROTESTS. This is a live domestic-instability channel; it is recorded here and is NOT used to move the regional-relapse or full-war lines, because the load-bearing part of it is single-stream. Separately, the Hormuz transit-fee article is NOT ENACTED — the National Security and Foreign Policy Committee approved Article 3, covering fees for navigation and environmental services, fuel supply, insurance and security, and the proposal still requires a full-parliament vote and Guardian Council review; there was no plenary vote 26–28 August. Note the name collision: the committee spokesman is EBRAHIM Rezaei and is a different person from SNSC Secretary MOHSEN Rezaei. Khamenei has been SILENT for a sixth consecutive day — an explicit negative, and the most consequential one in the domestic file, because it leaves unresolved which institution is executing settled policy. Pezeshkian spoke at the Islamic Unity Conference in Tehran on 27 August: Iran is “not in a weak position”, and “no Muslim country’s territory should be used against another Muslim nation”. Araghchi wrote to the UN Secretary-General on 26 August calling the US measures “an act of state and economic terrorism” — the first Iranian attempt to contest the campaign in a multilateral rather than bilateral forum. There is NO new IAEA statement on Iran; the standing position is no verification activities since 28 February and access denied to 20 declared sites, and AEOI head Eslami said on 26 August that the Agency’s failure to condemn the strikes “calls its competence and independence into question”.

channels.name: Maritime denial
channels.rationale: Day 182. JMIC Update 090 supersedes 089: cumulative confirmed incidents 96 → 97 on the 25 August strike, Hormuz SEVERE and every threat level marked “no change”, mine danger areas still active and NAVCENT named as the source of the current clearance coordinates. The scored annex counts are 6 vessels on 25 August and 5 on 26 August against the ~138/day all-transit baseline — 4.3% and 3.6%, about a sixth of the 25% test. Four other universes are published beside them and none is spliced: 37 US NCAGS-facilitated transits over the same 48 hours, Kpler’s 10 visible vessels on 26 August against its own ~15 average, Windward’s own pair of 12 and 8, and TankerMap’s 0 / 1 / 0. An announced corridor is not a verified reopening, and 090 advises that vessels can expect to be hailed and directed onto the Iranian route.

channels.name: Oil price shock

The upgrade gap NARROWED to $6.48 on the scored CO2 series and $5.30 on the active, from $8.06 and $7.16 — the first narrowing in three editions, and the sequence now reads 9.78, 8.43, 5.55, 5.21, 3.03, 7.73, 8.06, 6.48 across eight readings, five narrowings and two widenings. The downgrade price leg is $16.04 above $72.48 and WIDENED by $1.58 on the session: a rising Brent moves toward the upgrade and away from the downgrade, and this session did both. The basis check clears on both contracts and the July roll artifact remains an open methodological item.

channels.name: US inflation impulse
channels.rationale: The 5y5y forward closed 2.3182%, a SECOND consecutive close above the 2.30% level whose break fired this channel on 31 July, and 1.82 bp clear of it; there have been exactly two single closes below 2.30% in the regime, 13 and 25 August, and both were retraced inside one session. The documented downgrade is the 2.142% pre-war anchor and the gap WIDENED to 17.62 bp from 16.12. Ten-year breakeven compensation closed 2.3335%, 7.66 bp above its own anchor from 6.91, so the forward and the realised data converged on the same reading for the first time in this regime. July PCE printed +3.7% y/y on the headline with real spending flat and energy goods the largest positive goods contributor.

channels.name: Treasury stress
channels.rationale: The volatility leg is satisfied for an EIGHTH consecutive close at 69.86 — the longest run since 10 June–10 July — but by 5.14 points instead of 5.56, because MOVE ROSE 0.42. The yield leg fails by 19.31 bp, WIDENED from 16.71, and 19.31 bp is more than twice the largest single-session 30-year move since 1 August, so it is three or more sessions away. THE TWO LEGS BOTH MOVED AWAY IN THE SAME SESSION: that is a joint deterioration, not a rotation, and the rotation rule does not apply to it; the previous joint deterioration was 21 August. The whole curve sold off with the belly leading, on labour-market data and an auction, with the Gulf absent from the attribution for a second consecutive session.
channels.move: held (at max) — 19.31 bp against US-inflation’s 17.62; inflation was already the nearer leg and the distance between them widened from 0.59 bp to 1.69

channels.name: Political stress
channels.rationale: The scored AUTMUSAG series last printed a RESOLVED $4.83 on 25 August, 23 cents above the named $4.60 downgrade condition and 8 cents above the $4.75 trigger. Its 26 August cell backfilled at $4.83 — identical to 25 August — and is reported UNRESOLVED with no day-on-day asserted, with the honest qualification that a two-decimal series repeats values genuinely and the test discriminates less here than on a yield. The series is dark on 27 August and its 28 August value is PROSPECTIVE. AAA diesel’s run of FOUR consecutive war highs BROKE at $5.6183, and AAA regular is now below both its week-ago and month-ago levels — neither of which the scored series can see.

channels.name: Escalation risk
channels.rationale: A tanker was struck INSIDE the Strait on 25 August, published only on 27 August, unclaimed and unattributed, and it is that incident which moved the count 96 → 97. The White House said on the record that no negotiations are happening; Iran is drafting CONDITIONS and the IRGC restated its price. Two parties publicly setting preconditions on the day a mediator visits is a priced stalemate, not a stand-down, and an announcement is not an event. Against it, the kinetic case is the strongest recorded: a 30-day CENTCOM combat-release silence, 28 nights with no strike inside Iran, 8 with no Iranian ballistic launch and 9 with no drone launch — four clocks, never merged.

2026-08-28.scoreTotal: TOTAL 27 / 30 — CRISIS band (22–30), held for a FOURTEENTH consecutive edition. FIVE of six channels sit at the cap, so no deterioration can raise this number through any of them; the sole route up is the oil channel at 2, and it moved TOWARD its upgrade this session after two editions moving away. A flat 27 is therefore an artifact of the scale rather than a statement about stability, and the movement inside it is in the distance-to-trigger figures: US inflation 17.62 bp from its anchor and WIDENED, Treasury stress 19.31 bp and WIDENED, oil $6.48 from its upgrade and NARROWED, political stress 23 cents and unchanged. The composition this edition is that the market record improved on one leg and deteriorated on three, while the event record produced its clearest documentary contradiction of the war — and the total registered neither.

whatsChanged.title: 4 · What has changed since the 27 August edition
items: The American operational record contradicted the American political claim. JMIC Update 090, 27 August: mine danger areas still active, and clearance coordinates “available from NAVCENT NCAGS” — two days after the President said the mines were gone. It is an allied product carrying a NAVCENT referral, not a NAVCENT statement, and no US Navy or CENTCOM text on the claim has issued, so the dispute is narrowed rather than closed.

A tanker was struck INSIDE the Strait and the record of it appeared two days late. UKMTO Attack 121-26, issued 27 August for a 25 August event: AL SALAM II, eastbound near Khasab, projectile above the waterline, confirmed by the Omani Maritime Security Centre. Cumulative count 96 → 97. The corridor announcements of 26 August were made in the interval, unclaimed and unattributed.

Iran named a price instead of a route. Rezaei, 27 August, via Reuters: a LIST OF CONDITIONS is being drafted at the mediators’ request, “ending the regional war” among them, and a “designated central channel” opens only on US compliance. Third Iranian description in two days, two of them geometries and one a revenue claim; none has an Omani counterpart, because the only Omani text describes no geometry, fee or revenue share.

Qatar mediated in person and on an incompatible position, and a standing premise of this document is narrowed. The Qatari PM met Araghchi, Pezeshkian and Ghalibaf in Tehran on 27 August seeking a return to the pre-28 February status quo. The inherited claim that the un-issued joint declaration is “Qatar’s gate on all mediation” is NOT supported by this window and is cut back.

Washington disowned the track on the record. Leavitt, 27 August: “No negotiations are happening right now.” Operations named as Epic Fury and Economic Outcast; the blockade continues. Bessent’s financial-institution designation still has not issued — a third day — and the 27 August OFAC action is Venezuela-only.

The snapshot missed the whole US session in one direction and four readings failed with it. Brent settled $2.10 above the snapshot on CO2 and $2.47 on the active, and the 2–30y sector +1.03 to +1.76 bp; Henry Hub and TTF are EXCLUDED as restatement-contaminated. Brent ROSE $1.58, ending the down-run, and the oil gap NARROWED to $6.48.

Threshold B did not re-arm and the Treasury legs both moved away. 30-year short by 0.69 bp, the narrowest 30-year-leg miss recorded on a close; 10-year SATISFIED at 4.6762%. MOVE rose 0.42 to 69.86 — an eighth consecutive close below 75 but satisfied by less — while the yield leg widened 2.60 bp to 19.31. That is joint deterioration, not rotation.

A vendor RESTATEMENT, two BACKFILLS, and a record run that broke. Henry Hub and TTF restated UP across 24–26 August and nothing else restated; SOFR backfilled for 26 August at 3.64; AUTMUSAG backfilled at an IDENTICAL $4.83 and is therefore UNRESOLVED. AAA diesel fell 0.47 cents to $5.6183, ending four consecutive war highs.

The 7-year cleared and the dealer backstop run was mis-sorted in draft and corrected. $44bn at 4.512% on a 2.50 cover, dealers 12.264% of competitive-accepted — the SECOND-highest of the five-auction run, behind the 20-year’s 12.34%, not the highest. Directs 26.959%, indirects 60.777%.

The Jackson Hole programme was published on the evening of 27 August, correcting the last edition’s “NOT published”, and it contains no energy or oil-shock session — which confirms that edition’s inference from the theme rather than merely restating it. Warsh’s first keynote as Chair is 10:00 ET Friday 28 August and is PROSPECTIVE.

Initial claims fell to 203,000 with the prior week revised up to 207,000 and continuing claims down 18,000 to 1,778,000 — a labour market with no visible crack, which is the condition under which a September HIKE stays live. The advance goods trade deficit widened 17.2% to $118.8bn.

The SPR acquired a second published value that does not reconcile with the first. The DOE’s own Quick Facts page gives 294.1 MMB as of 20 August by site against the 289.7 mn bbl this monitor recorded; different series, different vintages, the weekly page unreadable because it is served as a JPEG. Both printed, no delta computed, neither withdrawn.

scenarios.name: Deal collapse — talks stall on terms
scenarios.desc: The strait stays shut not because talks failed to start but because the terms on offer are incompatible. Iran is now drafting a list of CONDITIONS rather than a route; the mediator in the room is working to a pre-28 February objective that negates the framework; and Washington has said on the record that no negotiations are happening.
scenarios.shift: +1 (42 → 43), modal for an eleventh consecutive edition, and the non-Tier-3 evidence is stated first. The White House said ON THE RECORD on 27 August that no negotiations are happening, and Qatar’s prime minister was physically in Tehran carrying a return to the pre-28 FEBRUARY status quo — an international waterway under the IMO traffic separation scheme, which is the negation of a jointly administered, revenue-sharing Strait. The three incompatible Iranian descriptions in two days are Tier 3 and corroborate rather than drive this.

scenarios.name: Return to full war
scenarios.desc: Sustained US or Israeli strikes inside Iran resume, or Iran attacks a Gulf state or US facility directly, and the shipping lane closes outright rather than being metered.
scenarios.shift: –1 (18 → 17), a FOURTH consecutive cut. FOUR non-comparable clocks, all longer: a 30-day CENTCOM combat-release silence, 28 nights with no strike inside Iran, 8 with no Iranian ballistic launch and 9 with no drone launch. JMIC 090 records no confirmed attack on shipping in any of its six other named regions in the period. The cut is small because the kinetic quiet is now well established and each additional night adds less than the last.

scenarios.name: Contained but violent
scenarios.desc: Attacks continue on shipping and on Gulf energy infrastructure at the current tempo, the blockade holds, transit stays in single digits, and no party escalates to a decisive move.
scenarios.shift: +2 (23 → 25), and the evidence is physical rather than rhetorical. A tanker was struck INSIDE the Strait on 25 August, published 27 August, unclaimed and unattributed, and the cumulative count moved 96 → 97. JMIC 090’s mine language is unamended and NAVCENT is named as the source of current mine-danger coordinates; 090 advises that vessels can expect to be hailed and directed onto the Iranian route; and three Houthi ballistic missiles struck Mocha port on 26 August with a fourth at Khokha on 27 August — land and port targets, never counted as maritime incidents, but part of the same tempo.

scenarios.name: Regional relapse
scenarios.desc: The conflict widens through the Red Sea, Lebanon, Iraq or the Gulf littoral, or Iran’s domestic position deteriorates far enough to change its external calculus.
scenarios.shift: Unchanged (9), deliberately, and the reasons now cut both ways. Arguing for a cut: SNSC Secretary Mohsen Rezaei re-emerged on the DIPLOMATIC track rather than the pipeline threat, and his 24 August naming of Saudi and Emirati bypass pipelines as targets remains unretracted single-stream Tier 3. Arguing for a rise: Iran’s fuel crisis is a live domestic-instability channel — two vice-presidents describing the position as impossible on the record, and a signalled price rise and rationing scheme within weeks against the precise trigger of the November 2019 protests. It is recorded and not scored, because the load-bearing part of it is single-stream.

scenarios.name: Mediated pause
scenarios.desc: A negotiated de-escalation restores partial transit under an agreed arrangement, with a verified reopening and traffic recovering toward a quarter of the pre-war baseline.
scenarios.shift: –2 (8 → 6), the first cut after two consecutive rises, and it is driven by an on-the-record denial rather than by absence. Qatar mediating in person is process; “no negotiations are happening right now” from the White House podium, on the same day, is the substance. Both parties published preconditions — Iran a list of conditions with the regional war’s end among them, the IRGC the lifting of the blockade plus compensation and sanctions relief. Still NOT talks: none convened, none scheduled, no timetable.

2026-08-28.scenarioShift: Four of the five lines moved and they sum to 100. Deal collapse and return to full war together carry 60%, UNCHANGED after two consecutive falls from the 67% high of 21 August — so the composition of that 60% has shifted toward collapse-on-terms and away from renewed war for a fourth straight edition. Four of the five scenarios still keep the strait shut, so 60% is NOT a label for “the strait stays shut”. Note the asymmetry deliberately: the scenario map moves on evidence the documented channel rules do not admit, which is why four rows shift on a session in which no channel did. The map is a probability assessment; the score is a rule-bound instrument, and they are not the same thing.
watchlist: Whether Threshold B re-arms on the 28 August close. The 10-year leg is satisfied on both the close and the intraday, and only the 30-year fails — by 0.69 bp on the close and 0.59 on the intraday. A re-arm would be the SIXTH arming and would follow a THREE-close lapse, so it would NOT be a one-session round trip; the three one-session re-arms since 29 July, the window in which the state sequence is counted, are 10, 14 and 20 August.

Whether the Treasury legs resume rotating or keep deteriorating together. 19.31 bp on the yield leg against a largest-single-session 30-year move since 1 August of 9.15 bp — three or more sessions away. The US-inflation leg REMAINS the nearer market downgrade candidate at 17.62 bp, as it was a session ago at 16.12 against 16.71, but it sits on a forward that has broken and retraced within a session twice.

Whether route COORDINATES are ever published, and whether OMAN publishes at all. Coordinates, not communiqués. Oman’s MFA has published no text on the corridor since the 25 August joint statement — verified against fm.gov.om directly for 26, 27 and 28 August. Watch fm.gov.om and ONA, and watch specifically whether Oman contradicts the IRGC revenue-sharing claim, which no Omani text supports.

Whether UKMTO Update 091 and VRA Overview No. 4 land, and whether the mine language survives them. 091 is due about 29 August and No. 4 was due 28 August; both are PROSPECTIVE, not unobtained. A NAVCENT or CENTCOM text addressing the presidential mine claim directly would settle what 090 only narrows.

Warsh’s first keynote as Chair, 10:00 ET Friday 28 August. The programme is now published and contains no energy session, so any oil-shock signal has to come from the opening remarks themselves. It lands into a 203k claims print and a live September-hike question, and Bessent’s designation, if it issues, lands on top of it.

Whether Brent holds the reversal and whether the transit counts move at all. The 28 August intraday gave back 39 cents of the $1.58. Quote both oil bases every time. On transits the test is whether the JMIC annex leaves single digits, and Baltic week 35 plus the 1 September GDPNow and EIA retail prints are the next scheduled reads.

Whether Bessent’s financial-institution designation issues and whether it reaches a Chinese bank. It did not appear on 26, 27 or 28 August despite a “before end of week” signal, and the September Xi state visit is reported as the constraint. Watch OFAC Recent Actions and the Federal Register.

Whether the UAE ever publishes an implementing decree, carve-out, licence regime or CBUAE circular — nine days and counting — and whether any US or CENTCOM statement ever corroborates the Emirati attribution of the 18 August missiles, now a tenth day.

Whether the SPR conflict resolves. Two published values on two vintages, 289.7 mn bbl against the DOE’s own by-site 294.1 MMB as of 20 August, with the weekly page served as an unreadable JPEG. The 2 September WPSR is the next scheduled chance to settle it.

Whether AUTMUSAG resolves at all. The scored series has one unresolved backfill, one dark session and one prospective print, and the political channel cannot move until it prints cleanly. Diesel’s war-high run has broken but the level is 19.76 cents from an all-time record the scored series cannot see.

protocol.detail: Never build an edition off a stale extract: check the file timestamp AND parse the sheet, because a stale timestamp and a stale row are different failures. This edition’s extract carries a 28 August row against the 27 August row the last edition ran on, so it is fresh. Parse with a dynamic header scan, auto-detecting the Brent and WTI front month and taking whatever label the scan returns for the dollar index. Re-verify the 27 February anchor field by field — done this edition, unchanged on all sixteen fields. Then run all THREE checks: the row-level stale check, the field-level exact-equality check, and the continuation-versus-active basis check. This edition: row and basis CLEAR, the field-level check FIRES on AUTMUSAG, SOFR backfilled, and Henry Hub and TTF were RESTATED across three sessions.

protocol.step: Compute deltas and test every trigger explicitly
protocol.detail: Day-on-day, week-on-week five rows back, and versus pre-war; explicit trigger tests for the four market channels plus the three Stage-4 thresholds. Label the two week-on-week bases separately when they diverge, as they do here — oil against 21 August on the intraday, rates against 20 August on the close. Run minimum, maximum and last-prior-occurrence on the full column before writing ANY superlative: it is what kept this edition’s TTF, MOVE and Threshold B claims honest, and two of the three were wrong in draft and caught by the harness.

protocol.step: Verify the news on both tracks and re-verify what was inherited
protocol.detail: Every claim needs a named source and an exact date, and negative claims decay faster than positive ones — an inherited, load-bearing negative about Qatar was re-tested this edition and cut back rather than repeated. State the exact query behind every negative. Say NOT OBTAINED rather than estimating, and distinguish NOT OBTAINED from PROSPECTIVE: Baltic week 35, VRA Overview No. 4, UKMTO 091, the 28 August AAA print and Warsh’s keynote are scheduled future events and are kept out of the not-obtained register.

protocol.step: Reconcile the previous snapshot and withdraw conclusions by name
protocol.detail: The Singapore-AM cut regularly misses the US session that sets the close, and the narrative conclusions built on it must be withdrawn by name rather than quietly corrected. The 27 August snapshot missed in ONE direction across energy, the dollar and the whole 2- to 30-year sector, and four readings were withdrawn: the three-session down-run and the “second consecutive widening” to $8.06; the intraday claim that the 30-year failed Threshold B by 1.73 bp; “the rotation rule is restored”; and “Henry Hub 7.22% below pre-war”, the one withdrawal the cut did not cause. A restatement contaminates a reconciliation the same way a carried field does, so the Henry Hub and TTF rows were EXCLUDED with the exclusion printed.

protocol.step: Score on confirmed closes, with hysteresis, and QA in three passes
protocol.detail: Never move a market channel on an intraday print; never whipsaw on a single session; never move a downgrade rule to match the level that fired the upgrade. Then run three QA passes, in order: a numeric harness recomputing every figure against the parsed dataframe; an adversarial PROSE pass by a reviewer with no access to the source data, run TWICE because the fixing introduces its own defects; and a VISUAL render, which is not optional. This edition ran 253 numeric checks, re-run after the prose fixes, and the harness caught two of the author’s own superlatives before either reached a reader. Two adversarial prose passes returned roughly a hundred and then twenty-six defects, several of the second round created by fixing the first — including a doubled verb, a duplicated sentence and an unbalanced markup tag that stopped the renderer.

methodology.scale: Shock-score scale. Six transmission channels (maritime denial, oil, US inflation impulse, Treasury stress, political stress, escalation risk), each 0–5, summed to 0–30. Bands: 0–7 watch · 8–14 stress · 15–21 systemic-risk watch · 22–30 crisis. Market channels move only on a confirmed close through a trigger, never on an intraday print — which is why the 28 August snapshot in this edition moves nothing. Maritime denial and escalation risk are event-based and move on events, not announcements: a declared posture, a stated objective, an issued framework, a set of announced corridor parameters, a list of conditions or a mediator’s visit is not an event. Hysteresis is asymmetric by design: a channel is upgraded on a sustained break of its trigger and downgraded only on a sustained reversal past a wider threshold, and the rule is never moved to match the level that fired it. It was vindicated again this edition: the 5y5y forward broke below its own firing trigger on 25 August and has now closed ABOVE it on two consecutive sessions. It is the second single-close break of that level to be reversed on the very next close, after 13–14 August, and had the channel moved on the 25 August close it would have been wrong within a day for the second time in a fortnight. One open item remains disclosed rather than decided: the oil channel’s downgrade is written as a mediated pause AND “a close” at or below $72.48, while its upgrade requires a SUSTAINED break — as written, the downgrade is easier to trip than the upgrade, which inverts the hysteresis principle. The condition is $16.04 away and is not live, so the asymmetry is disclosed rather than settled under time pressure.
methodology.scaleCap: The saturated scale. FIVE of the six channels are at 5; only oil, at 2, is not — three points below the cap, not one. Deterioration cannot raise this score through any of the five, and the sole remaining route up is the oil channel, which this session moved TOWARD its upgrade after two editions moving away. A flat score is therefore an artifact of the scale rather than a statement about stability. This edition is a seventh variant of the problem and the variant is a split between the market record and the event record. The market record deteriorated on three legs and improved on one: the Treasury yield leg widened 2.60 bp to 19.31, the US-inflation gap widened to 17.62 bp, the volatility leg was satisfied by less at 69.86, and only the oil gap improved, narrowing to $6.48. The event record produced the clearest documentary contradiction of the war — an allied advisory recording mine danger areas as still active and referring shipping to NAVCENT for coordinates, two days after the President said the mines were gone — alongside a tanker struck inside the Strait, a mediator in Tehran on an incompatible objective and an on-the-record American denial that any negotiation exists. The total registered neither. Readers should attend to the composition and to the distance-to-trigger figures, which are reported in basis points and dollars precisely so that movement inside a frozen total remains visible: 17.62 bp on US inflation, 19.31 bp on Treasury stress, $6.48 on oil, 23 cents on political stress.

The rule is applied anyway, because the cost of under-claiming for one session is trivial and the distance to the $4.60 condition is 23 cents on either reading. Six series have no 28 August print (Asia LNG, MOVE, VIX, SOFR and both gasoline series) and are reported BLANK rather than carried. Verification ran 253 independent recomputations against the parsed dataframe, re-run AFTER the prose corrections, and the harness caught two of the author’s own superlatives in draft — a TTF close written as third-highest when it is second, and a MOVE close written as third-lowest of its phase when it is fourth. methodology.intraday: Intraday caveat, and a note on the section references. Numbered references of the form §9.n in the PDF edition point to the monitor’s internal operating instructions and pitfalls register, which records every failure mode the process has hit since June and the rule adopted in response; they are not sections of the published document. Two entries were added to that register by this edition. The first is that a restatement contaminates a reconciliation and the contaminated rows must be excluded by name. A reconciliation gap is the snapshot minus the close, so if the close has been restated the gap mixes a timing miss with a restatement and measures neither — the same failure the register already forbids when a field has been carried rather than refreshed. Two further consequences follow whenever a restatement lands and both occurred here: a war-record level can move without a market move, as the TTF record close did, and a headline percentage can move without a market move, as Henry Hub’s discount to pre-war did. Both must be disclosed as restatements rather than reported as market news. The second entry is that an identical-value test has a precision it is written for, and this one is written for four decimals. AUTMUSAG backfilled at $4.83, identical to the previous session, and the rule was applied — but on a two-decimal retail series that repeats values genuinely, an exact repeat carries almost none of the improbability the rule relies on. The rule was applied anyway because nothing turned on it, and the honest form is to say so rather than present a near-certain false positive as a catch. On the data itself: the latest dated row is a Singapore-AM snapshot and US hours set the close; the error is regime-dependent rather than random and has ranged from thirteen cents to $3.99 on Brent within a fortnight. This edition’s reconciliation of the 27 August cut missed in ONE direction across every field measured, which is the pattern that most often falsifies a de-risking narrative, and four readings were withdrawn by name in consequence. At the ten-year point the move split, with about 0.80 bp of real yield and the balance compensation — the reverse of the previous session, when the whole ten-year move was compensation — so the session is decomposed rather than labelled. Series go dark for multiple sessions and backfill later, sometimes at values indistinguishable from a carry. A row can fail to refresh entirely, an individual field can carry forward inside an otherwise live row, a continuation series can break silently across a contract roll, and a vendor can restate a whole series across a multi-session window. Every one of these failure modes has occurred since 29 July, each is tested for explicitly on every run, and the results of those tests are published rather than assumed.

2026-09-01.headline: Score HOLDS at 27/30 for a sixteenth consecutive edition. No channel moved. Iran answered the Larak strike by firing ballistic missiles at American bases in JORDAN, and three foreign ministries — Jordan's, Iran's own and Qatar's — put it on the record inside twenty-four hours, turning the last edition's uncorroborated Tier 3 claim into a Tier 1 event. One. What is corroborated is the EVENT, not the damage. Petra reports eight missiles intercepted and destroyed and gives no launch total, so no interception rate follows from it; Iran's foreign ministry confirms the targeting; Qatar names Iran, and names the UAE with it. Against that, ABC carries two Jordanian security sources saying some missiles were NOT intercepted, no US or Jordanian damage assessment or casualty figure was OBTAINED, and the separate UAE strike claim is Iranian and DENIED by Abu Dhabi. Trump promised retaliation and had not delivered it at the cut — the largest open fact on the board, and the reason the full-war line moves two points rather than ten. Two. The allies would not certify the mine claim. JMIC Update 091, issued after Adm. Cooper declared the internationally recognised routes free of Iranian mines and on the day of the Larak strike, re-published 'mine danger areas still active' and continuing clearance operations, both flagged '(No change)'. Four allied statements inside a week now say the lanes are clear, that no ship has hit a mine, that launchers were loading fresh ones, and that the danger areas remain. Only the FLOW-not-STOCK reading fits all four, and it rests on allied paper rather than on this document's inference. Three. The market half moved in the right shape and cost two downgrade legs. A BEAR STEEPENER rising monotonically with tenor took the 10-year to 4.7500% and the 5-year to 4.5002%, both NEW WAR-HIGH CLOSES, on real yield rather than compensation, and Threshold B held a second close with both legs widening. A channel scored at 5 on a trigger that has now failed twice running is the most adverse fact here for the monitor's own scoring, and §9.26 still forbids moving the rule. Four, and nobody has priced it: the 60-day War Powers clock from the 10 July notification expires on 8 SEPTEMBER, into a Senate sitting in pro forma session until 14 September. A statutory expiry arrives six days before the chamber that would have to act can act. Sequencing 27 → 27 → 27. Five of six channels are at the cap, so the score can register NEITHER an Iranian ballistic-missile attack on American bases in a treaty partner NOR two war-high Treasury closes on one day.
